title: Rational smooth models and finite-stage factorization of regular fibre maps
statement: Let $k$ be a characteristic-zero field. A principal singularity pair $(X,I)$ means an affine finite-type $k$-scheme $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], an ideal $I=(\pi)$ with $\pi$ a non-zero-divisor, and $X_{\mathrm{sing}}\subseteq V(I)$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Write $X_m=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^m)$ and $I_m=I\mathcal O_{X_m}$. Maps of pairs preserve the distinguished ideals by extension. There is a small directed inverse system $(X_a,I_a)$ of affine finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes with principal non-zero-divisor ideals and singular loci contained in $V(I_a)$, whose inverse limit as pairs is $(X,I)$. All transition maps are affine smooth maps preserving the ideals, and all projections from $X$ are regular [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism]. For each $m\geq1$, $X_m=\varprojlim_a X_{a,m}$, and the fibre projections are regular. The same holds for finite disjoint unions, allowing different fields on different components. Moreover, choose such a system for another principal singularity pair $(Y,J)$ over a possibly different characteristic-zero field and fix a target index $a$. Every regular map of pairs $h:(Y_m,J_m)\to(X_m,I_m)$ has the following finite-stage factorization: for some source index $b$, the composite $Y_m\to X_{a,m}$ factors as $Y_m\to U_m\xrightarrow{v_m}X_{a,m}$, where $U$ is an open neighborhood of the image of $Y_m$ in $Y_b$, $U_m=U\cap Y_{b,m}$, and $v_m$ is a smooth $\mathbf Q$-morphism preserving the distinguished ideals. Increasing $b$ is permitted, while $a$ remains fixed. No lift of $v_m$ to $U\to X_a$ is asserted.

proof.text: Choose the coefficient system $k=\varinjlim R_a$ from [lem-per-char-zero-smooth-coefficient-system]. The ring $A$ has a finite presentation over $k$: apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation], since a field is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$). By [lem-kun-fp-algebra-descent] there is $a_0$ and a finitely presented $R_{a_0}$-algebra $A_0$ with $A=A_0\otimes_{R_{a_0}}k$. Lift the finitely many coefficients of a polynomial representing $\pi$ to a common later coefficient ring; replace $a_0$ by that index and $A_0$ by its base change. We now have $\pi_0\in A_0$ mapping to $\pi$. For $a\geq a_0$ put $A_a=A_0\otimes_{R_{a_0}}R_a$ and let $\pi_a$ be the image of $\pi_0$. Every $A_a$ is a finite type $\mathbf Q$-algebra. The tensor-element colimit statement [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] shows $A=\varinjlim A_a$: ring multiplication agrees on the tensor generators, so the module universal property is the ring universal property as well.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, first paragraph; finite-presentation model with its chosen equation, expanded using Stacks 05N9.

proof.text: For $a'\geq a$, the map $A_a\to A_{a'}$ is the base change of the smooth inclusion $R_a\to R_{a'}$, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] (so the transition morphism of spectra is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]) and flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. The Noetherianity of $R_a$ and $A_a$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], starting with $\mathbf Q$. For a fixed $a$, the tail diagram thus consists of smooth $A_a$-algebras with colimit $A$. The ring $A$ is Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma over $k$; each fibre of $A_a\to A$ is a quotient of a localization of $A$, hence Noetherian. Therefore [lem-per-smooth-colimit-regular] makes $A_a\to A$ regular. Its scheme map is regular by the fibrewise definition [def-per-regular-scheme-morphism]. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] identifies scheme and ring flatness; [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] upgrades the purely inseparable test for a regular ring fibre to the finite-extension test in the scheme definition.

Make $\pi_a$ a non-zero-divisor at a stage. At the current initial stage put $N=\ker(\pi_a:A_a\to A_a)$. This is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite]. The smooth coefficient transitions are flat, and $R_a\to k$ is flat by [lem-per-char-zero-smooth-coefficient-system]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] identifies $N\otimes_{R_a}k$ with the kernel of multiplication by $\pi$ on $A$, which is zero by hypothesis. Apply [lem-pc-finite-tensor-vanishing-colimit] to a finite list of $A_a$-module generators of $N$, regarding them as elements of the $R_a$-module $N$. At a common later coefficient stage all these generators have zero tensor image. They generate the base-changed module, so that module is zero. Applying the same flat exactness lemma identifies it with the kernel of multiplication by $\pi_b$ on $A_b$. It follows that $\pi_b$ is a non-zero-divisor. Every subsequent stage retains this property by flat exactness. Restrict to this cofinal tail.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, descent of the principal non-zero-divisor ideal; kernel descent expanded.

proof.text: The open $X\setminus V(\pi)=\operatorname{Spec}A[1/\pi]$ is regular by the hypothesis on the singular locus. The field $k$ is perfect: all its algebraic extensions are separable by [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable]. Hence [lem-trf-regular-perfect-field-smooth] makes this open smooth over $k$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] the ring map $k\to A[1/\pi]$ is smooth. Fix the current initial coefficient stage $a$ and apply [lem-sbc-smooth-pushout-filtered-colimit-stage] to the finitely presented map $R_a\to A_a[1/\pi_a]$ and the coefficient diagram $R_b$, $b\geq a$. Its limit base change is exactly $k\to A[1/\pi]$; the tensor identification sends $x/\pi_a^n\otimes r$ to $r x/\pi^n$, with inverse induced by the universal properties of tensor and inversion. We obtain $b$ such that $A_b[1/\pi_b]$ is smooth over $R_b$. It remains so at all later stages by smooth base change. Compose with the smooth $\mathbf Q\to R_b$ using [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. This ring map is smooth, and by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local] the open complement of $V(\pi_b)$ is regular. Restricting to this tail gives the required singular-locus condition on every model.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, ensuring every rational model is a principal singularity pair; smooth open descent via Stacks 0C0B.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$ put $A_{a,m}=A_a/(\pi_a^m)$. A compatible family of maps $A_{a,m}\to C$ is exactly a compatible family of maps $A_a\to C$ killing $\pi_a^m$; the latter corresponds to a map $A\to C$ killing $\pi^m$. Thus $A/(\pi^m)=\varinjlim A_{a,m}$ as rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] the corresponding spectra form the asserted limit, also for $m$ omitted. Extension of $(\pi_a)$ gives $(\pi_b)$ and $(\pi)$ by construction. The transition $A_{a,m}\to A_{b,m}$ is the base change of $A_a\to A_b$, since $A_b\otimes_{A_a}A_{a,m}=A_b/(\pi_b^m)$, hence smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition], and its spectrum morphism is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. The limit $A/(\pi^m)$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and its fibre rings over $A_{a,m}$ are Noetherian by localization and quotient. Apply [lem-per-smooth-colimit-regular] again to get regular fibre projections. The indexing sets are small; pass to a common universe containing both sets and rings before using any tensor-colimit node. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] identifies scheme and ring flatness; [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] upgrades the purely inseparable test for a regular ring fibre to the finite-extension test in the scheme definition.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, thick fibres of the approximation; quotient universal property and Stacks 01YW, 07EP.

proof.text: Fix $a,m$ and a regular pair map $h:Y_m\to X_m$. Write $C=A_a/(\pi_a^m)$ and $B=\Gamma(Y_m,\mathcal O)$; let $t\in C$ be the image of $\pi_a$. Fix a source index $b_0$ and a generator $\sigma_{b_0}$ of its distinguished ideal; for $b\ge b_0$ let $\sigma_b$ be its image in $B_b$, which generates the extended distinguished ideal, and let $s\in B$ be its image, a generator of $J_m$. The composite to $X_{a,m}$ corresponds to $f:C\to B$. The pair condition gives $u,v\in B$ with $f(t)=su$ and $s=f(t)v$. Form the finitely presented $\mathbf Q$-algebra $E=C[S,U,V]/(t-SU,S-tV)$. Here $C$ is finitely presented because it is finite type over the field $\mathbf Q$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Send $S,U,V$ to $s,u,v$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-algebra-factors-filtered-colimit] to $E\to B=\varinjlim_b B_b/(\sigma_b^m)$, where $\sigma_b$ is the chosen source generator. At the resulting stage the image of $S$ and $\sigma_b$ have the same image $s$ in the colimit. By the zero-detection assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise], with the base ring $\mathbf Q$ and tensor factor $\mathbf Q$, their difference becomes zero at a later stage. The two displayed equations then show $(f_b(t))=(\sigma_b)$ there. Thus the descended map $g:Y_{b,m}\to X_{a,m}$ is a morphism of pairs, and $gp_b$ is the original composite. All indices enlarged are source indices; $a$ is unchanged.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, finite-stage factorization (corrected arrow direction); Stacks 00QO, pair equations included.

proof.text: Both $p_b:Y_m\to Y_{b,m}$ and $q_a:X_m\to X_{a,m}$ are regular by step 5. Thus $gp_b=q_ah$ is regular: on affine rings apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-composition]; its composite fibre rings are Noetherian because the target algebra is $\Gamma(Y_m,\mathcal O)$, a Noetherian ring. The finite-stage $\mathbf Q$-morphism $g$ is locally of finite presentation: on rings its target algebra is finite type over its source algebra (the finite list of rational generators still generates), and both are Noetherian, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation] applies. Now [lem-per-regular-precomposition-smooth-image] gives an open $W\subseteq Y_{b,m}$ containing $p_b(|Y_m|)$ on which $g$ is smooth. Since $Y_{b,m}$ is the closed subscheme $V(\sigma_b^m)$ of $Y_b$, its topology is the subspace topology. Choose an open $U\subseteq Y_b$ with $U\cap Y_{b,m}=W$. The image of $Y_m$ lies in $W$, so the map factors through this open by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme]; set $U_m=W$ and $v_m=g|_W$. Equality of the principal ideals persists after restriction. Smoothness is only asserted for $v_m$, not for a lift on $U$. The affine flatness criterion [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] identifies scheme and ring flatness; [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-regular-finitely-generated-extensions] upgrades the purely inseparable test for a regular ring fibre to the finite-extension test in the scheme definition.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.5, final shrinking paragraph, using Lemma 2.1.4; fixed target index and source-side open.

proof.text: For a finite disjoint union, apply steps 1--5 to every component and take the product of their directed index sets. At a product index use the disjoint union of the component models; this is affine because a finite union of spectra is the spectrum of the product ring. Ring maps out of a product correspond to orthogonal idempotents summing to one: their images in a filtered ring colimit lift to a common stage, and the finitely many equations $e_i^2=e_i$, $e_ie_j=0$, $\sum e_i=1$ hold at a later stage by the same finite-presentation factorization and zero-detection nodes used in step 6. This also proves that limits of these finite disjoint union systems are the desired union. Smoothness and regularity can be checked on its open-and-closed components from their local definitions. For a map from a union of source components to the fixed finite target union, step 6 applies directly to the finite product coordinate rings, so no component-preserving assumption on $h$ is needed. Steps 7 then apply to that descended map and the whole source union. Empty unions and empty thick fibres use the zero ring and the empty open; all the assertions remain valid.
